business: The Aldera: magnesium in single-serve capsule sachets (pure bisglycinate and a 3-form complex)
target: US adults 28-55, mostly women, who buy magnesium on Amazon, compare price per serving and read reviews

segments.name: Prime replenisher who reorders the same bottle

behaviours.name: Compares price per serving
behaviours.how: Sorts by price, divides by servings, knows Nature Made 200 mg costs about $0.39 a day.

behaviours.name: Reads the 1-star reviews first
behaviours.how: Will not buy without hundreds of reviews and checks complaints about pill size, stomach and fake dosing.

behaviours.name: Loyal to a known brand
behaviours.how: Takes Pure Encapsulations, Thorne or Nature Made and trusts NSF or USP seals.

behaviours.name: Subscribe & Save regular
behaviours.how: Puts staples on monthly auto-ship and rarely switches.

behaviours.name: Wants third-party testing
behaviours.how: Looks for NSF, USP or lab reports, distrusts unverified claims.

behaviours.name: Hates big pills
behaviours.how: Left bad reviews on huge capsules, prefers small pills or powder.

behaviours.name: Travels and packs pills in a pill case
behaviours.how: Counts capsules into a weekly organizer or zip bag before trips.

objections: $1 a serving when Nature Made or Double Wood cost $0.20-0.40
A new brand with zero reviews
Size 00 capsules are hard to swallow
'200 mg' turns out to be two capsules
Magnesium complexes with citrate give me stomach cramps or diarrhea
Anyone can print 'lab-tested'; I trust NSF or USP
I already have a magnesium that works for me
habits: you have Subscribe & Save for several vitamins
you take magnesium at night with your other supplements
you fly for work every few weeks
your doctor suggested magnesium for sleep or leg cramps
you keep a weekly pill organizer on the bathroom counter
you read Amazon reviews for 20 minutes before buying anything new
you keep a few things in your car and gym bag so you never forget them
you have tried three magnesium brands this year
